To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a gene expression system designed to express multiple genes in different subcellulat locations in plants has been tested and shown to be effective.
we have developed a gene expression system that can be used to co-ordinate the expression and subcellular location of multiple genes in plant cells.
the Nla gene from the tobacco vein mottle virus can be used to generate polyproteins that are processed to yield multiple, functional proteins in plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a gene expression system designed to co-ordinate expression of multiple genes with the targeting of their products to specified subcellul locations.
the design and construction of a series of genes that are able to express and target multiple genes to different compartments in plant cells.
the development of a gene expression system designed to allow coordinated expression of multiple proteins, each targeted to a specified subcellular compartment, in plant cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a polyprotein containing the Nla protein of TVMV, and the genes for the chloramphenicol acetyltransferase and acetate kinase, is a good system for the expression of multiple genes, and for targeting of proteins to the chloroplast.
the use of the Nla protein as a protease for the processing of polyproteins is a useful tool to engineer plants.

the polyproteins were processed in the cytoplasm, the chloroplast, the peroxisome and the mitochondria, and in all cases except the chloroplast, they were processed in the order in which the enzymes appeared.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Nla protease can be used as a tool for the expression of multiple genes, and the targeting of their products to the chloroplast, in plants.
we have developed a strategy to co-ordinate the expression of multiple genes, and that we have shown that this strategy is effective in plants.
we have shown that the Nla gene from tobacco vein mottled virus (TVM) can be used to co-ordinate the expression of multiple genes and their subsequent targeting to different subcellular locations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Nla protease can be used in cis to express, as separate polypeptides, two or three different genes, and that these polypeptides can be targeted to the same or different subcellular locations.
we can express multiple enzymes, each with its own subcellular localization, in the same plant cell.
the TVMV Nla protease can be used in the context of plant gene expression systems to express, in the correct subcellular compartment, multiple proteins that may be encoded by a single gene.
